r01.binding_source: praśraya / praṇāśa — giving latitude to the point of dissolution; unrestrained indulgence that runs to annihilating collapse
r01.instructions: Author one neutral English paraphrase per pole: preserve meaning + valence; no Sanskrit term; no transliteration; no letter/sound reference; avoid candidate glosses and near-synonyms; uniform noun-phrase form; comparable length.
r01.liberating_source: disciplined containment that holds form — latitude restrained and sublimated so the dissolving tendency is contained rather than annihilating

r02.binding_source: the inflated 'I did / I control this' — the 'I'-feeling swollen into sole doership (as in Aurangzeb: 'had I not been there the world would have been destroyed')
r02.instructions: Author one neutral English paraphrase per pole: preserve meaning + valence; no Sanskrit term; no transliteration; no letter/sound reference; avoid candidate glosses and near-synonyms; uniform noun-phrase form; comparable length.
r02.liberating_source: agency exercised WITHOUT inflating the 'I' — acting and functioning while not claiming sole doership

r03.binding_source: mūrcchā — hypnotic entrancement, the loss of common sense / discernment under the spell of a ripu (deluded obsession that suspends judgment)
r03.instructions: Author one neutral English paraphrase per pole: preserve meaning + valence; no Sanskrit term; no transliteration; no letter/sound reference; avoid candidate glosses and near-synonyms; uniform noun-phrase form; comparable length.
r03.liberating_source: breaking the entrancing spell into clear sense — withdrawing the mind (pratyāhāra) along the path of righteousness, no longer spellbound (aided by kīrtana / devotional song)

r04.binding_source: envy — the sting at another's success; covetous resentment at another's good fortune
r04.instructions: Author one neutral English paraphrase per pole: preserve meaning + valence; no Sanskrit term; no transliteration; no letter/sound reference; avoid candidate glosses and near-synonyms; uniform noun-phrase form; comparable length.
r04.liberating_source: muditā — sympathetic gladness at another's fortune; rejoicing in others' good rather than being stung by it

r05.binding_source: ensconcement gone rigid — over-holding, clinging to one's holding; stuck fixity that resists the movement toward subtlety
r05.instructions: Author one neutral English paraphrase per pole: preserve meaning + valence; no Sanskrit term; no transliteration; no letter/sound reference; avoid candidate glosses and near-synonyms; uniform noun-phrase form; comparable length.
r05.liberating_source: dharma — ensconcement in one's original (true) stance; the sustaining principle ('that which sustains'), the unbroken movement toward subtlety and merger into Parama Puruṣa (mānava dharma)

r06.binding_source: kruratā — cruelty: physical harm inflicted on the weak; crude, cruel thought and behaviour
r06.instructions: Author one neutral English paraphrase per pole: preserve meaning + valence; no Sanskrit term; no transliteration; no letter/sound reference; avoid candidate glosses and near-synonyms; uniform noun-phrase form; comparable length.
r06.liberating_source: compassion (karuṇā) that protects the vulnerable — the counter-measure to cruelty; the will to reduce another's misery and help arouse their latent intellect

r07.binding_source: aviśvāsa — self-doubt that cannot commit: lack of confidence and wavering ('shall I be able to do it?'), distrust of self and others
r07.instructions: Author one neutral English paraphrase per pole: preserve meaning + valence; no Sanskrit term; no transliteration; no letter/sound reference; avoid candidate glosses and near-synonyms; uniform noun-phrase form; comparable length.
r07.liberating_source: self-efficacy — the confidence to commit and to rely: steady trust in oneself, others and the path

r08.binding_source: peevishness / reactive irritability — perverse, contrary reactivity discharged at others (taking offence at kindness, calm under harshness)
r08.instructions: Author one neutral English paraphrase per pole: preserve meaning + valence; no Sanskrit term; no transliteration; no letter/sound reference; avoid candidate glosses and near-synonyms; uniform noun-phrase form; comparable length.
r08.liberating_source: forbearance that absorbs provocation — an even, unreactive temper that does not discharge irritation

r09.binding_source: restless striving that cannot stop — effort compulsively driven on, unable to cease (and, clung to mundane ends, ceaseless outward striving)
r09.instructions: Author one neutral English paraphrase per pole: preserve meaning + valence; no Sanskrit term; no transliteration; no letter/sound reference; avoid candidate glosses and near-synonyms; uniform noun-phrase form; comparable length.
r09.liberating_source: will-force applied to arouse one's dormant higher potential — purposeful effort that exerts and then rests into poised, alert repose without inertia; the effort behind spiritual elevation

r10.binding_source: kāma — worldly / physical desire and longing: grasping for wealth, opulence, name, fame, social position; the tamasic pull toward the crude
r10.instructions: Author one neutral English paraphrase per pole: preserve meaning + valence; no Sanskrit term; no transliteration; no letter/sound reference; avoid candidate glosses and near-synonyms; uniform noun-phrase form; comparable length.
r10.liberating_source: physical longing sublimated / redirected toward the higher — desire turned from kāma toward mokṣa (the longing for liberation); worldly grasping released

r11.binding_source: avajñā — neglect / disregard of what actually has value; indifference misapplied so that genuine worth goes unattended
r11.instructions: Author one neutral English paraphrase per pole: preserve meaning + valence; no Sanskrit term; no transliteration; no letter/sound reference; avoid candidate glosses and near-synonyms; uniform noun-phrase form; comparable length.
r11.liberating_source: regard that recognizes and attends to worth — giving due attention to what has value (and reserving indifference/upekṣā only for the truly unacceptable)

r12.binding_source: mamatā bounded by the relative factors (time, space, individuality) — partial, possessive 'mine-ness' that clings to its own (own child, own country, own moment) while excluding or even harming what lies outside it
r12.instructions: Author one neutral English paraphrase per pole: preserve meaning + valence; no Sanskrit term; no transliteration; no letter/sound reference; avoid candidate glosses and near-synonyms; uniform noun-phrase form; comparable length.
r12.liberating_source: mamatā made to TRANSCEND time, space and individuality — love expanded past its relative boundaries into universal affection that holds the loved on an open hand (achievable only by human beings, through persistent, intense effort)

r13.binding_source: cintā as anxious rumination — the mind churning over unresolved contingencies and personal consequences (e.g. worrying through the late-train inconveniences), gripping the what-ifs
r13.instructions: Author one neutral English paraphrase per pole: preserve meaning + valence; no Sanskrit term; no transliteration; no letter/sound reference; avoid candidate glosses and near-synonyms; uniform noun-phrase form; comparable length.
r13.liberating_source: cintā as composed, impersonal reflection — holding an unsettled situation open without forcing premature closure; objective contemplation in which one is 'not a direct player' (e.g. weighing how a failing industry might be revived), reflection without anxious grip

r14.binding_source: the sentient / sattvic impulse clung to — clarity, purity or harmony owned as superiority or attachment (the subtle 'golden chain' of spiritual attainment)
r14.instructions: Author one neutral English paraphrase per pole: preserve meaning + valence; no Sanskrit term; no transliteration; no letter/sound reference; avoid candidate glosses and near-synonyms; uniform noun-phrase form; comparable length.
r14.liberating_source: mokṣa — unqualified liberation; sentient clarity realized WITHOUT attachment to it ('clarity without attachment to clarity')

r15.binding_source: outward / visible vision — fixation on the manifest, physically-seen, outward-facing world
r15.instructions: Author one neutral English paraphrase per pole: preserve meaning + valence; no Sanskrit term; no transliteration; no letter/sound reference; avoid candidate glosses and near-synonyms; uniform noun-phrase form; comparable length.

r16.binding_source: āśā as grasping / clinging hope — goaded toward a specific outcome or object; the downward pull of attached desire
r16.instructions: Author one neutral English paraphrase per pole: preserve meaning + valence; no Sanskrit term; no transliteration; no letter/sound reference; avoid candidate glosses and near-synonyms; uniform noun-phrase form; comparable length.
r16.liberating_source: aspiring hope held WITHOUT attachment — forward-orientation that acts while releasing the grip on the result (oriented toward the Great, not the object)

r17.binding_source: artha as possessive acquisition — worldly purpose pursued and possessed as acquisition, status or control (rajasic grasping to acquire)
r17.instructions: Author one neutral English paraphrase per pole: preserve meaning + valence; no Sanskrit term; no transliteration; no letter/sound reference; avoid candidate glosses and near-synonyms; uniform noun-phrase form; comparable length.
r17.liberating_source: purposeful action without possessive bondage — rajasic energy directed to legitimate purpose/means without clinging (artha pursued without attachment)
